review: The hymn is creation and redemption answering each other: 1:1–6 is Ps 19:2 (הַשָּׁמַיִם מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד־אֵל) with Exod 3:14 (אֶהְיֶה), 2:1–6 is 1 John 4:9–10 with Phil 2:7 (הֲרֵיק) and John 1:29, 3:1–6 is Luke 22:44 with Mark 14:36 and John 12:3 (the feet), and 4:1–6 is Isa 64:5 with Song 1:12 (נֵרְדְּ) and Rom 12:1.

1:6 אֶהְיֶה הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנִּשָּׂא — the Arabic أَهْيَه الْعَظِيمَ الْأرْفَعَا transliterates the divine name of Exod 3:14; the Hebrew gives it as אֶהְיֶה, the form the verse itself uses, and keeps the two adjectives of the Arabic, so the confession is the Name and not a title.
1:1–2 are one sentence broken by the print; the Hebrew keeps the break after אֲשֶׁר, as the Arabic breaks after الَّتِي, so the couplet still runs on into 'on earth and in heaven together'.

4:6 וְאֶת־נִרְדֵּנוּ הַיָּקָר — the Arabic وَنَارِدِينِنَا الثَّمِين is 'our precious nard'; the Hebrew keeps נֵרְדְּ, the spice of Song 1:12 and 4:13, because the stanza is the anointing of the feet and the ointment must be the real one.
